body:
Might be worth clarifying what "path" means here (with an example?). Especially the fact that the path may contain only single slash (so e.g. `parent/name`). If there is no slash, the shortcut will display under a category with its name (e.g. `name` will be displayed as `name/name`), while more slashes will be ignored (`parent/name/surname` will display as `parent/name`).

Another thing is that custom shortcuts with unassigned events will not be saved in editor settings, so you need to add them every time. Seems like `add_shortcut()` handles it properly if added shortcut already exists. Usage example would be useful.
This should only happen if the shortcut has no name already.

This is not used anywhere, so you could remove it.
Unless...
Should we prevent removing built-in shortcuts?
@KoBeWi I'd prefer being able to remap keys without limitations on the builtin keys

This is used to prevent platform overrides, since we shouldn't be overriding something a user did intentionally.
